Serve opens a delivery API and sandbox for its robot fleet

Developers can test quotes, dispatch and tracking; live deliveries require approval and remain limited to supported service areas.

The Robot Report ↗11 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

Opening access to an operating fleet

Serve Robotics has launched its AV Delivery Developer Portal for developers and AI agents. It exposes delivery services using Serve’s existing fleet. This is distinct from the earlier Physical AI Services offering, which supplies connectivity and data technology for other companies’ machines.

A delivery workflow through an API

Applications specify pickup and drop-off points, request a quote, dispatch a delivery and track progress. Serve handles fleet assignment, routing, navigation and remote supervision. A sandbox lets developers test workflows and edge cases before connecting to real deliveries, separating application development from direct robot control.

Live access remains conditional

Production access requires Serve’s approval and depends on operating areas, service hours and cargo restrictions. A public portal does not mean robots can be requested in every city. The source’s third-generation robot video provides hardware background; this story does not announce a new robot generation.
